clue.text: Some travelling round in groups to get basic education

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Children taken round on group outings pick up a basic schooling along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'to get' into the definition, but the noun is just 'basic education'; 'to get' only links it to the wordplay. 'Some' picks the letters out of 'travellinG ROUND IN Groups'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounding is the fundamental training in a subject, the foundation that later learning builds on.

clue.text: Broadcast set out again for an audience

explanation.walkthrough: RELAID (laid out again) and RELAYED sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal passed on and transmitted to listeners has been relayed, that is, sent out over the air.

clue.text: At university good person getting mature and superior

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means haughty or snobbish, putting on airs above other people.

clue.text: Good past making one happy

explanation.definitionFit: A digraph is a pair of letters representing one sound, such as ph or sh.

clue.text: The French General with record no one acclaimed

clue.text: See groups backing Conservative in small rooms

explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means brave and undaunted by danger.

clue.text: Learner being kept in that is least likely to make an effort

parts.note: the bacterium's name supplies its letters as written

clue.text: Laze around in endless postprandial rest? Most disgraceful!

explanation.surface: Lounging about in a never-ending after-dinner snooze is shameful!

clue.text: Most meagre home for bird on meadow

clue.text: Little son acting badly and making false pretences

clue.text: Proposal sent electronically creating strong feeling?

D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
